criteria.criterion: A unit test in crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs builds a line whose earlier attempt ended on low disk and shows evaluate_before_attempt gives no T1/T2/T5 pause or flag from it, while the same line with a Rejected verification does. Run: cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard.
criteria.evidence: I ran the command and `environment_stop_is_not_counted_but_a_rejection_is` passed. The test builds two Environment attempts, with 240 minutes in total, plans growing from 4 to 9 and planning round T2_PLANNING_ROUND. evaluate_before_attempt gives Level::None for T1 through T5. The same line built with Rejected attempts gives T1 Flag, T2 Pause, T4 Pause and T5 Pause. The test would fail without the change: without `counted()` and the Environment variant, line A reaches the same levels as line B. The watcher test `a_low_disk_job_is_read_as_an_environment_attempt` also passed. It runs a real ask/go through `low_once_verifying`, gets an outcome reason starting `environment:` and Verdict::Environment, and writes no pause or flag file.

criteria.criterion: A unit test in scope_guard.rs shows a retry that resumes a kept candidate (planning, build and checks done) is judged against the cost of its remaining stages: spend that would pause as a fresh job does not pause, and the same spend on a non-resuming retry does. Run: cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard.
criteria.evidence: `resumed_retry_is_judged_on_remaining_stages` passed. A stopped attempt costing 1.4 followed by a resumed attempt costing 0.1 gives spend 0.1 against forecast 0.3 and Level::None. The same costs with resumed=false give spend 1.5 against forecast 1.0 and Pause. A resumed attempt costing 0.5 still pauses, and one costing 0.35 flags, so T3 stays active. In the end-to-end watcher test a real `athena retry` after low disk lands, and request_records reads it with resumed=true.

criteria.criterion: The existing scope_guard tests (t4_pause_via_go_and_ask, retry_refuses_paused_line, t3_pause_from_reading_forecast and the rest) still pass, so real rejections and cost overruns still pause lines. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded check passed: `cargo test --locked`, 1537 tests. In my targeted run, t4_pause_via_go_and_ask, retry_refuses_paused_line, t3_pause_from_reading_forecast and the other 23 scope_guard tests passed. The only change to the existing fixtures is `resumed: false` in the `att` helper.

criteria.criterion: cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings are clean.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks on this tree both passed: `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry naming the scope guard change: environment-ended attempts are not counted, and resumed retries are forecast on remaining stages.
criteria.evidence: There is a new bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Fixed`. It names the scope guard and says environment-ended attempts are not counted toward T1, T2 or T5. It says a resumed retry is compared with 0.3 of the cost p90, marked as an estimate. It also names the root cause (`attempt_of` treated every non-landed, non-rejected job as failed) and job 20261028-034820-v3rf.

criteria.criterion: Each new constant or rule in scope_guard.rs has a doc comment stating its basis or marking it an estimate, and the diff touches only crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs and CHANGELOG.md.
criteria.evidence: Each new item has a doc comment. ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX cites its basis, disk::LOW_DISK, and a test ties the two. PRODUCER_SHARE and VERIFIER_SHARE are marked 'Estimate, not measured'. Verdict::Environment, the `resumed` field, `counted`, `t3_basis` and `resumed_candidate` each say what they do and on what basis. `git diff HEAD~1 --stat` lists only CHANGELOG.md and crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs.

findings.summary: A usage-limit stop is still counted as a failed attempt.
findings.evidence: Searching crates/ finds no code that records a usage-limit stop with an `environment:` reason. The new rule therefore covers low disk only: interrupted jobs are mostly never counted because they stay Dispatched, which attempt_of skips, and usage limits are not covered at all. The CHANGELOG says this openly: 'a usage-limit stop once it is recorded that way'. Changing how outcomes are recorded is out of scope, so the next step is a follow-up job that records usage-limit stops with the prefix.

findings.summary: T3 now ignores what an environment-stopped attempt spent when its work was kept, even if that spend was far over the forecast.
findings.evidence: `t3_basis` drops a kept Environment attempt's cost from spend, and that applies to the T3_LINE_DOLLARS flag too. An attempt that spent many times p90 and then hit low disk raises no T3 signal on its line. This follows the accepted reading ('spend already made on the kept stages is not counted against it'), but the guard loses sight of a real overrun.

findings.summary: A planned test case was dropped: a retry that ran a producer is never shown to be read as not resumed.
findings.evidence: The plan named a fixture where a retry with a Producer invocation gives resumed=false. Only the true case is exercised, end to end. The false path in `resumed_candidate` is not shown to fail when it should.

summary: The change does what the request asks, and the verdict is pass. The scope guard now treats a job that closed failed with a reason starting `environment:` (low disk today) as an environment stop. Those attempts no longer count toward the attempt, round or time signals; a rejected verification still counts. A retry that resumes a kept candidate is now compared with the verifier's share of the cost forecast (0.3 of the p90, an estimate). I ran `cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard` in this snapshot and all 26 tests passed, including three new ones. Two of them compare an environment stop with a rejection and a resumed retry with a fresh one. The third runs a real low-disk ask, go and retry end to end. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs (1537 tests) passed. Only CHANGELOG.md and scope_guard.rs changed, and every new constant has a doc comment giving its basis or marking it an estimate. Three findings are left for later. A usage-limit stop still counts as a failed attempt, because nothing records it with the `environment:` prefix yet; the CHANGELOG says so. T3 no longer sees what a kept environment-stopped attempt spent, even if it ran far over the forecast. The planned test showing that a retry which ran a producer is not read as resumed was dropped.
